From cb9e0e5006064a807b5d722c7e3c42f307193792 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Keith Busch <keith.busch@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2019 10:56:43 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] nvme-pci: use blk-mq mapping for unmanaged irqs
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

If a device is providing a single IRQ vector, the IO queue will share
that vector with the admin queue. This is an unmanaged vector, so does
not have a valid PCI IRQ affinity. Avoid trying to extract a managed
affinity in this case and let blk-mq set up the cpu:queue mapping instead.
Otherwise we'd hit the following warning when the device is using MSI:

diff --git a/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c b/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
index 599065ed6a32..f562154551ce 100644
--- a/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
+++ b/drivers/nvme/host/pci.c
@@ -464,7 +464,7 @@ static int nvme_pci_map_queues(struct blk_mq_tag_set *set)
 		 * affinity), so use the regular blk-mq cpu mapping
 		 */
 		map->queue_offset = qoff;
-		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL)
+		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)
 			blk_mq_pci_map_queues(map, to_pci_dev(dev->dev), offset);
 		else
 			blk_mq_map_queues(map);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/nvme/host/pci.c`**
   - The condition in the `if` statement at line 465 was modified. The original condition `if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL)` was changed to `if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)`. This modification adds an additional check for the `offset` variable, ensuring that the `blk_mq_pci_map_queues` function is only called if both conditions are met.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `pci.c` addresses a specific scenario where a device is using a single IRQ vector, which is an unmanaged vector. By adding the check for `offset`, the code avoids attempting to extract a managed IRQ affinity when it is not applicable. This change allows the block layer (blk-mq) to handle the CPU-to-queue mapping correctly, thereby preventing warnings related to IRQ affinity extraction when the device is using Message Signaled Interrupts (MSI). The relationship between the modification and the bug fix is that it directly prevents the warning and potential misconfiguration of IRQ handling in the NVMe driver.

Reported-by: Iván Chavero <ichavero@chavero.com.mx>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs when a device provides a single IRQ vector that is unmanaged, leading to an attempt to extract a managed IRQ affinity, which is not valid. This results in a warning during the IRQ handling process, particularly when using Message Signaled Interrupts (MSI). The code was incorrectly trying to map the IRQ affinity without considering the unmanaged nature of the IRQ vector, causing the system to hit a warning in the `pci_irq_get_affinity` function.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int nvme_pci_map_queues(struct blk_mq_tag_set *set)
 {
 	struct nvme_dev *dev = set->driver_data;
 	int i, qoff, offset;
 
 	offset = queue_irq_offset(dev);
 	for (i = 0, qoff = 0; i < set->nr_maps; i++) {
 		struct blk_mq_queue_map *map = &set->map[i];
 
 		map->nr_queues = dev->io_queues[i];
 		if (!map->nr_queues) {
 			BUG_ON(i == HCTX_TYPE_DEFAULT);
 			continue;
 		}
 
 		/*
 		 * The poll queue(s) doesn't have an IRQ (and hence IRQ
 		 * affinity), so use the regular blk-mq cpu mapping
 		 */
 		map->queue_offset = qoff;
-		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL)
+		if (i != HCTX_TYPE_POLL && offset)
 			blk_mq_pci_map_queues(map, to_pci_dev(dev->dev), offset);
 		else
 			blk_mq_map_queues(map);
 		qoff += map->nr_queues;
 		offset += map->nr_queues;
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
